rows.TEXT: In his youth, this mighty lord once stood fast against an army from hell and single-handedly defeated them by sealing the gateway that spew them. He then became sovereign of his realm.

Highest lord of the dwarf lords, he is known for his intensity in battle and his courage in the face of overwhelming odds. He once fought seven days and nights against the mighty red dragon ARFURUZON to finally defeat him.

Known in his times as the mightiest of all adepts of the black art, this lord was slain by the inquisitor Vorgel who ended his reign of terror. He is now resurrected as an undead with the intention to subjugate every mortal to his will.

Serphis 
"The Merfolk may be Solonielle's children, but they are no friends of ours. We can expect trouble as we pass through their waters."
"I'm more concerned about the Humans on the other side. These sea creatures are wild and unorganized. The Humans are expecting us."

Dwarf King 
"The Elves! I was wondering when all this standin' around would end. Finally, some entertainment!"

Dwarf King 
"Save some for me, cousin!"

Grizzlespit 
"That oughtta do it! Let's see just how sturdy this gate is. Everybody duck!"

Grizzlespit 
"WHAT? I CAN'T HEAR YOU LAD, MY EARS ARE RINGING!"

Defender of the Faith 
"They've entered the valley! Do not let them pass!"

Grizzlespit 
"That's what I needed. Bring me to the gate at the Valley of Justice. I will blow that thing right out of its hinges!"

Fyrwenn 
"That did it! We're moments away from victory! Charge the city!"

Tora'ach 
"That's what we wanted to hear!"
Defeat Sir Allemon and Gumtik Bledwater.

Gumtik Bledwater 
"A good fight, lads! She'll be needing some fine tuning before she's ready to see combat again!"

Millu 
"No...see here? He backed into a tunnel system. Did you hear that thump? What was it?"

Tora'ach 
"My guess would be the Dwarf just sealed the end of the tunnel. We should hurry to the city before they try to flee with the Clavis!"

De'elkil 
"It's true, then! You are moving to reclaim Temperance! How can we deny the call of our god?"

De'elkil 
"We...obtained...this from a traveller who wandered into our forest. Just holding it will fill you with a terrible rage. We were waiting for some way to safely dispose of it, but perhaps you are more worthy."
"What a foul thing. Yet it feeds so much energy into my being. We will see to it that this relic is destroyed when Temperance is ours."

De'elkil 
"Do you have something for us? Bring it forward. Otherwise, begone."

De'elkil 
"What's this? You wear an enemy symbol in our presence? Die!"

Illumielle 
"You fools! These Elves offer their help and you slay them?"

Orummell 
"Ah, yes. So you are the ones we have been hearing about. How can we deny the call of Gallean? We've been waiting for a chance to reclaim Temperance for a very long time."

Orummell 
"I am a simple leader of a small tribe. I think these will be much better used with one of you. May they bring you as much luck as they have for me."

Illumielle 
"You fools! Why do you attack those who offer their support? We'll never have the numbers to accomplish our task!"

Orummell 
"You dare wear the enemy's pendant among our ranks? You will not survive this insult!"

Orummell 
"From the queen? Perhaps you have something that will prove it? Bring it to us."

Serphis 
"I don't like this place. We're much too confined...we're easy targets with nowhere to flee if we're outnumbered. I'll be thankful when we're in open forest once again."

Thuume 
"Elves! Your assault will only slaughter your own people! This is a meaningless battle! Why do you persist in this insanity? Go back to your forests, you will NOT march upon Temperance!"

Serphis 
"This wizard may pose a problem. No doubt he will use his magic to hold us back before we can get close enough to put an arrow through him. Perhaps we should use some of our own magic to counter him before we advance?"

Watchman 
"Look! Angels descend from the observatory! They seek to claim our land while we are away, no doubt."

Scout 
"M'Lady, there is a pass leading directly into the heart of enemy territory, but we were unable to breach it. There's a massive iron wall blocking our advance!"

Grizzlespit 
"An iron wall isn't  much of a problem if I can find the components needed to blast her down. A few scrapings from dragon dens will do fine."

Illumielle 
"Dragons? We've no time for this! And how much is a "few?" We must move before the Empire is fully prepared!"

Grizzlespit 
"Two. Get me two and I will manage. Any sort of salt or slime will do. When you find them, bring them to me and I will concoct a nice little surprise for that gate. I won't be responsible for what happens once it's down though!"

Scout 
"The gates to Temperence are locked!"

Nedrem 
"There were two keys forged, one for the Humans and one for the Elves. Once Emry left Temperance, the Humans kept both keys for themselves."

Scout 
"We have seen Dwarves enter the city with siege machines. They had no Human escort."

Nedrem 
"They must have given our Clavis to the Dwarves to speed up reinforcements! Treachery! The Dwarven territories have no protective borders, we should retrieve what is ours!"

Nedrem 
"The Clavis! We have found it! This will open the gates of Temperance!"

Illumielle 
"At last, we are upon the borders of Temperance! Gallean has carried us this far, and still presses us forward! We've lost many, and gained new allies as well. Even a handful of Wotan's children stand beside us!"

Grizzlespit 
"A Dwarf is always true to his word. We're here to repay our debt is all."

Illumielle 
"Perhaps our Oracle has something for us before we make our final march? Please, Millu, step forward."

Millu 
"I won't lie to you. From the beginning, my visions have shown great loss to all during this battle. We must trust that there is reason behind Gallean's will. We must trust that he guides us to new prosperity!"

Millu 
"In one ear, he weeps for our suffering. In the other, he screams for retribution! We have been treated unjustly by the Humans. Our place of peace became a stronghold for their greed! Gallean promises us the return of Temperance!"

Scout 
"The Strait of Solonielle to the south ends very close to the walls of Temperance, but its waters are full of beasts."

Fyrwenn 
"No doubt the Empire guards their end of it well."

Scout 
"Or perhaps that is what they expect us to think?"

Scout 
"There is a northern bend that will lead us closer to Temperance without bringing our armies too near its walls. However, it will send us through the center of the Dwarven reinforcements."

Grizzlespit 
"I do not like that plan."

Spiritess 
"Quickly, get the Dwarf to safety. I was unable to save the others."

Spiritess 
"You fought well. For now, you must rest. We will take Grizzlespit to a safe place while he heals."

Watchman 
"The Dwarves are hoping we've left our cities unsecured! We must protect them or they will close in from behind!"

Grizzlespit 
"Bah! Who needs a key? Step back!"

Sir Allemon 
"They've destroyed the gate! To your places, men! Do not let them near our city!"
Defeat Sir Allemon and Gumtik Bledwater.

Forest Liege 
"The citizens of the area will not simply let us push through their lands. They will not be as well trained as the Empire soldiers, but they will quickly become an annoyance. Perhaps we should leave a force behind in case they rebel?"

Murgres 
"I hope you've left your wounded under protection...let us see, shall we?"

Gladeshadow 
"M'Lady, I've been inquiring as to the...loyalty...of the Elves in this region. They have heard of our movement and think us an embarassment. Perhaps we should avoid them?"

Illumielle 
"We certainly have no time to demonstrate miracles again to win their trust. We will not be able to avoid them all. We do still have the pendant - perhaps it will win us some allies here."

Gladeshadow 
"And the ones who won't join us?"

Illumielle 
"They stand in the path of their god. We will not tolerate further distractions; there is no time left. If Elves stand against Gallean, they will not be spared. It is a sad reality, but we have no choice."

Gladeshadow 
"Soon the Humans will be hunting them as well...they will no doubt declare war on all of our kind."

Imperial Assassin 
"Wait...do not be alarmed. We are not here for violence. Please, be seated...there is someone who wishes to speak with you."

Illumielle 
"Ambrielle! I wish we'd meet under better conditions. Does Emry know you are here?"

Ambrielle 
"Of course not. The king prepares for war. That is why I am here. Why are you proceeding in this madness? Why destroy everything we have worked to accomplish? These attacks are unwarranted!"

Illumielle 
"You of all people should be aware of the injustices the inhabitants of Temperance have committed upon my...our...kind!"

Ambrielle 
"What injustices? Keeping Elves out of the council? We both know Elves are creatures of the wild...what good will they do in Temperance? Elves belong in the forests, not in our cities."

Illumielle 
"How can you say that? We share the same bloodline! How can you ignore Gallean's call?"

Ambrielle 
"Can't you see it? Gallean has gone mad! I serve two gods. The Highfather does not order his people to their slaughter. Please, call this off! You are the queen, you can stop this!"

Illumielle 
"As are you. Leave, before I call my sentries."

Spearman 
"We always thought the Elves a noble people. How mistaken we were..."
"We could say the same thing about you."

Troll 
"This place not for you! This for worship Gromdok!"
"Gromdok? Is that the name of their foul diety?"

Sentry 
"Divine avatars of the Highfather...I never expected to see one, let alone slay it. This seems so surreal."
"They were here for a reason...this tome seems a thing of miracles!"

Primitive Giant 
"You think we let you just walk in and take it??? Gaaaah!"

Trapper 
"It's true, then! The Elves are invading these lands. This is no longer a safe place for our tribes."
"Quickly, scrape the walls for residue. The Dwarf may be able to use it!"
"Collect a small amount of the slime in those pools. The Dwarf said he could use it. Be careful, it will burn you!"

Squire 
"You'll answer to the King for this!"
"The King has much to answer for himself."
"Disgusting. There are flies and rotten food everywhere. How could anyone live in this place?"

Demmeic 
"Ah, there you are! Well met, I am Grizzlespit's brother, Demmeic. I suppose I owe you my thanks for reminding the Clans that they are warriors. There will be civil war, no doubt, but in the end it was the right thing to do."

Tora'ach 
"We could care less about Dwarven politics. What is it you want?"

Demmeic 
"Calm down, boy. Don't drive off your allies, even if they are temporary. This won't be an easy fight for you and I am offering my help. I am to meet with Dwarves of...similar goals. They will fight for you if you'll have them."

Tora'ach 
"Dwarven reinforcements...how strange. Where must you go?"

Dimmeic 
"They await our arrival at the Urbress Training Grounds. If the Dwarves who were loyal to the queen find them there, they will be executed. We must not let that happen."

Demmeic 
"Come out if you're still here lads!"

Gubber 
"I'll be damned! You made it! Let's get out of here before we're discovered!"
"We're attacking churches now? Is this really Gallean's will?"

Watchman 
"M'Lady, there is an old Elf in the woods outside the city who claims he needs to speak with you. He says his name is Nedrem."

Illumielle 
"Nedrem! I haven't heard that name for a while. Please, escort him in at once!"

Nedrem 
"Ah, there you are...I bring news from the northern forests, my queen. Your message has wound its way deep into every forest on Nevendaar. Thousands of Elves march this way."

Illumielle 
"That is wonderful news, but I cannot take credit for the message. We both know who gives us direction. You look well, Master. I miss our studies together."

Nedrem 
"As do I, M'Lady. Though I suspect I have nothing left to teach you. You would be amazed to see the power of the little ones now. With Gallean's presence, they are much more focused."

Illumielle 
"Please, stay with us for now. I would not risk losing you on your journey back. When this is done, we will provide an escort to see you safely home."

Scout 
"By Gallean, look at the road behind Temperance! There is an army marching this way! The Empire's reinforcements will be here soon!"

Serphis 
"Blue Dragons. They were once Solonielle's most loyal servants. No wonder they tolerate the sea people being so close to their lair."
"Look at the demons scattered about the floor! They're dying! Let us hope it is the same all over Nevendaar. Perhaps we've finally seen the end of Bethrezen?"
"Apparently these beasts have been dining on the local Elves. Burn this unholy place."

Sir Allemon 
"We have been bested! Where were the reinforcements?"

Gumtik Bledwater 
"King Emry fled! I saw his battallions retreat when the Elves moved past the walls. The Clans will hear about this! We failed because of Human cowardice!"

Sir Allemon 
"King Emry simply picks his battles, Dwarf. He must have realized he would have been throwing away the lives of his men. A valid assessment, it would seem..."

Serphis 
"Have these two executed. Clear out the remaining Humans, but do not harm the workers. We may require more hands to rebuild this city. I want sentries posted along the walls; we've won a great victory, but we must be careful."

Illumielle 
"Millu? Has anyone seen the oracle?"

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Ah...you are the ones causing all of this commotion. I won't be of any use to you in battle, but perhaps I can entertain your troops with my stories? Return here each day and I will share them with you."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Ahhh, you've returned for a tale. Perhaps you'd like to hear The Birth of History?"

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"The Highfather was so proud of his first angel, Bethrezen, that he bestowed to him the power of creation. Eager to prove the gift was not wasted, Bethrezen set out to construct the perfect world."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"He named this world Nevendaar, a sacred word in angelic tongue. When Nevendaar was young and its surface was but a blank canvas for the will of the Gods, Bethrezen urged the others to help him populate it."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"First, he chose the Lovers, Solonielle and Gallean. Gallean reached deep into the soil and vast trees began to stretch towards the sky. A reminder, he said, that his love for her overshadowed everything in the world."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Solonielle wept, her shining tears falling towards Nevendaar in a rain that would last years; for mortal centuries are but a minute for a God. Oceans soon painted the surface of the world, but they were incomplete."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Together, the Lovers seeded the world with their people. The trees cracked open and from their hollows emerged the Elves, keepers of the forests. Merfolk were born in the depths of the sea."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Wotan struck the world with his hammer, causing the ground itself to ripple into enormous mountain ranges. He introduced his honorable Dwarves to the surface of Nevendaar. To his surprise, they began tunneling into the ground."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Bethrezen, eager for children of his own, brought mankind to Nevendaar, as well as the animals to serve them. Men were fascinating to the Gods; their independence was unprecedented, their actions unpredictable."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Anything they desired was given to them by their father, and the world became a true paradise. However, worried that mankind needed his guidance, Bethrezen asked his fellow Angels to watch over their progress."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Bethrezen set out to share his creation with the Highfather and left Nevedaar under the care of his jealous brothers. However, that is another story. Return tomorrow and I will share it with you."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"The story of Bethrezen is a sad one, indeed. I'm glad you've decided to hear it, but he was not the only god to suffer. This tale I call the Birth of War."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"The Angels were jealous. While Bethrezen was away, they visited the world of man, and put his existence into perspective. Soon greed gripped the hearts of Bethrezen's children."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Man began to horde his possessions, waging war on those in the way - including the Elves.  The beauty of Nevendaar was insignificant next to the horrors committed by mankind."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"The Highfather gazed upon Bethrezen's world with disgust.  Was this some sort of mockery? Such an atrocity could not go unpunished, and the he banished Bethrezen to the filthy core of his own world."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Unable to avenge his own betrayal, the fallen god created a twisted race of demons to scour the world, bringing justice to the humans who had ruined it. Hatred fueled his minions, but they waited for mankind to weaken itself."

Ellowin the Storyteller 
"Instead, they focused their attention on the peaceful Elves. The great forests were set ablaze and Gallean's children were forced to flee them. Their path led them into the vast mountain ranges of the Dwarves."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Sensing invasion, the mighty Dwarves charged forward with weapons drawn and slaughtered hundreds. Gallean and Solonielle challenged Wotan. How could he let his Dwarves commit such senseless killing?"

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Gallean demanded that Wotan punish his murderous "half-men" for their treachery. Offended, Wotan plunged his fist deep into the forest god's chest, tore out his heart, and hurled it into the sun."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Horrified, Solonielle braved the intense heat to retrieve her husband's heart. Solonielle was severely burned, but she had succeeded. However, it was not enough. Gallean twisted and screamed in pain, but would not wake."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Of course, such a powerful being would have her revenge, but that is another story. A story I plan to tell tomorrow."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Where were we? Ah, yes...I was going to tell you all about the Age of Retribution..."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Solonielle's exposure to her suffering lover soon drove her mad. No longer was she keeper of the Elves, she had become Mortis - the fleshless goddess. She began to slaughter whole cities and resurrect them for her undead army."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Her first act was to hunt and slay the Dwarven king, for Wotan surely deserved to suffer. But this was not enough.she needed Gallean by her side. Together, they would make all of Nevendaar answer for their pain."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"A chance to heal him soon came in the form of a human child tainted by demonic corruption - Uther. With the retrieval of Uther's blood, Gallean was reborn. The blood had returned his handsome form as well as his noble spirit."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"He looked upon poor Mortis, his lost lover, and felt pity. She had become a beast; little remained of the soul he once loved.  Gallean left Mortis."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Our father had returned. Many of you know this tale, and many of you were a part of it. Return tomorrow and I will finish this long history of Nevendaar."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Before we move on to a new tale, we should finish the one we started. This is the Return of Gallean..."

Ewollin the Storyteller
"The Elves rejoiced at the return of their father. Overjoyed to see his children still survived, he sent them his own avatar Lachla'an. Lachla'an would spread a message of peace to unite those races in Nevendaar deemed worthy."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Mortis would not allow it. She arranged Lachla'an's death and brought him back as her own child, a twisted reflection, a Dark Elf. She used Lachla'an to taunt her husband into interfering directly with the ways of mortals."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"His wrath manifested as a corruption of nature and destroyed many people of all races. For but a moment, Gallean had felt the hatred that had corrupted his wife.  Appalled by his own actions, he sank into isolation, as did we."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"And here we are. We're writing history even now, though I am sure your march will be more noteworthy than an old man telling tales. I may have a few more to tell...return tomorrow and perhaps I will speak about the Centaurs."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Ahh...I have an audience, I see. Let's begin then. Right, the Centaurs. They are our noble protectors and loyal friends, but how did such magnificent creatures come to be?"

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Gallean saw that his Elves had a tendency to spread throughout the forests instead of amassing into cities as the other races did. They soon became independant societies with different ideals and ambitions."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"This was not what Gallean had intended, so he sought a way for them to communicate to all reaches of the woods. With help from Bethrezen, who created the beasts of Nevendaar, he constructed a much more agile creature."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"The Centaurs shared the same father with the Elves, just as the Merfolk shared the same mother. The Centaurs quickly delivered messages between the Elven groves as well as protected the forests around them."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Thus our guardians began their long friendship with our people. I see some of you in the crowd today. I am honored by your presence. Return tomorrow for another tale. Gromdok? Now that is an interesting story..."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Gromdok...yes, I do know a tale about that filthy god. He certainly isn't one of the original deities and only the Greenskins even believe in his existence."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"The story I have heard points to the beasts as their original forms. When the intelligent races were flourishing and using the animals as a source of food, fur, or labor, a creature that called itself Gromdok emerged."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"He was angry with the beasts. While the Humans and Dwarves were building vast cities, the beasts accomplished nothing. He urged them to become something else, and by willing it, actually transformed a number of them."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"If this Gromdok actually existed, he must have been some sort of powerful magician to do such a thing, for surely if he were a God he would be mentioned in our writings - or the writings of any other race."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"His people began to breed, and the results were slightly more intelligent with each generation, but also more and more deformed. The results, as it is told, are the Greenskins we know now - feral, nasty creatures."

Ewollin the Storyteller 
"Hard to believe, yes...but it does make an entertaining story, doesn't it? I have told enough stories, you must get on with what you are doing. I fear a horrible battle draws near. One day I will be telling your stories."

Demmeic 
"Tell my brother that though he may have regrets about his choices, I stood by him until the end. Wotan will welcome him...as he now welcomes me."

Gumtik Bledwater 
"Well, well! It took you long enough! I can tell you're not here to chat, but I'll let ole' Thunderguts do the chattin'! PREPARE MY MACHINE!"
"There it is! Tear down its walls!"

Sir Allemon 
"I don't know what madness has overtaken you Elves, but I will not allow you to harm the innocents within these walls! Send forward your champions. Let us see what honor you have left!"

Gumtik Bledwater 
"By Wotan, you shall be buried outside these walls!"
We can teach you spells of the darkest nature.
You wish to learn that which has taken us years of research?
Birng 'em in. They won't be the same when they return to you.
They seem weak from travel, but I think I can work with them.
I found them in the far north...they're quite friendly when you pay them well.
We'll march by your side to Temperance, but it will cost you.
You have a fine eye for value. Let's negotiate.
Nothing fancy here, but we'll keep your troops alive.
They may look like simple gems, but they will prove themselves in battle.
Potions of protection...you won't find them this cheap anywhere else.
